I am currently 35 years old, and I have been very angry for most of my life. In my dark moments I have allowed my anger to destroy relationships, shatter opportunities, and in general, make life harder for myself. This has been something I've struggled with for a long time, and although I don't have any easy answers for you, here is some advice that has made my life better.

I start each day with a koan over at /v/koans. I find this starts my day in the right mindset. Worth noting, I get up early- I like to be alone after I first wake up, and getting up early makes this easier.

I have found that spending 15 minutes for some quick yoga (or if you prefer, "stretching") followed by some meditation is a great way to follow my daily koan.Worth noting: I am not at all religious in terms of belief (agnostic atheist) but I find routine and tradition can be soothing.

After this: exercise. THE most important factor of my day. Be it weights or the bike or a quick set of surfing, I need to go make my heart beat hard for awhile.

I return from this in a great place to work- physically exhausted but mentally focused. Since I am a programmer, and sit in a chair all day, this little routine has helped me "get into the zone" more quickly.

I have also made a major change in my life this year regarding diet. I follow something paelo-ish, I've learned to cook, and more importantly, how to shop. Plants and meat; shit out of a box or bag or other package is almost always bad for you. This has made a profound change in my mood, and my wife's too.

I've been with my wife 13 years now, and earlier this year we were fighting like never before and even discussing divorce. It was a dark time for us. There is no easy answer, but my solution was to own my decision to be married. It is a choice to be married, and just like any other friendship, it requires work and patience and ongoing effort. Going tit-for-tat will solve nothing, but if one of the parties can swallow their ego for a few days, usually the other will stop being shitty too.

More general advice: I still get flashes of anger all the time, for no reason whatsoever. With practice it has become easier to recognize irrational anger (yelling at my dog for doing something dog-ish, like eating his bed) versus valid anger (being offended by some shithead who legitimately wronged me). And although I'd be lying if I said I have less anger now, I have learned to channel that anger, via exercise and creative pursuits, into something less destructive.

Good luck to you, brother.

I heard something once that really changed my perspective on anger. A friend told me, "Anger is the result of unfelt feelings." Meaning that something must first be suppressed before it turns into anger. An example would be that something happens at work. There is a new initiative pushed down from upper management that you don't agree with. You become angry at them and then the inner dialogue gets going on what they did wrong, how stupid the decision was, etc.

When we look at this scenario from a wider view, it would seem that this person feels unimportant because they were not consulted before the decision was made. They might feel disregarded or even taken advantage of. These are tough things to deal with emotionally. Most of us would rather suppress these feelings than acknowledge them. After they are suppressed, they turn into anger. So anger becomes a way for us to avoid uncomfortable feelings.

Another example could be between lovers. Let's say one cheats on the other and the relationship is compromised. The one who stayed faithful will be confronted by deep feelings of betrayal and abandonment. These are really tough to deal with. So instead of acknowledging these feelings, they become angry and focus this intense energy back on to the one who hurt them.

Not sure if this is at all helpful, but it has been proven true in my life many times. If I am getting angry, I try to see the situation objectively and investigate whether or not I'm trying to avoid some difficult feelings.
